discovery: Establishing molecular astrophysics as a quantitative probe of star and planet formation, tracing the physical and chemical evolution of matter from interstellar clouds to planet-forming disks

nominees.name: Ewine F. van Dishoeck
nominees.affiliation: Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, The Netherlands

subfield: Astrophysics - star and planet formation, astrochemistry
motivation: Ewine van Dishoeck turned molecular spectroscopy into a precise physical tool for following how stars and planets form. She combined laboratory and quantum-chemical data on photodissociation and excitation with radiative transfer. Using infrared and submillimetre observatories from ISO and Spitzer to Herschel, ALMA and JWST, she then measured temperatures, densities, ionisation and ultraviolet fields in collapsing clouds, protostellar envelopes and protoplanetary disks. Her work on photodissociation regions, water through the full star-formation sequence (Herschel WISH), ice inventories and disk snowlines showed how molecules, including complex organics, survive or are transformed on their way into planetary systems. She also led major instruments, including JWST-MIRI. Her results changed our picture of the physical conditions under which planets, including our own Solar System, are born and of what they inherit. She has defined and led this field for four decades.
